name: Zion Narrows
unique: A hike up the Virgin River between canyon walls a thousand feet high and sometimes twenty feet apart, with water at your waist and no trail at all.
buzz: Rent the canyoneering shoes and a walking stick; flash floods are lethal and rangers close it. Start early and go upstream.

name: Angels Landing
unique: A knife edge ridge with chains bolted into the rock and 1,000-foot drops on both sides, ending on a summit that feels like the top of the world.
buzz: The permit lottery is the hard part; people with a fear of heights turn around at the first chain section and that is fine. Go at dawn.

name: Arches National Park
unique: Two thousand natural stone arches, including Delicate Arch standing alone above a bowl of slickrock, in a landscape of fins, balanced rocks and red desert.
buzz: Timed entry in summer and parking is a fight; Delicate Arch at sunset is worth the crowd. Carry more water than you think.

name: Bryce Canyon
unique: Hundreds of orange hoodoos packed into a natural amphitheater, best seen from Sunrise Point at dawn or from the Queen's Garden trail down among them.
buzz: The amphitheater at sunrise is one of the great American views; the rim is easy and the trails drop fast. It is cold at 8,000 feet.

name: Park City Skiing
unique: The largest ski resort in the United States, with 7,300 acres, a historic mining main street and the Greatest Snow on Earth.
buzz: Terrain suits everyone from beginners to experts; the town is walkable and the ski-in access is rare. Book rentals early.

name: Goblin Valley
unique: A valley of thousands of mushroom shaped hoodoos you can wander among freely, with no trails and no barriers, a natural playground.
buzz: People call it the most fun park in Utah; kids climb everything and the light at sunset is unreal. It is remote.

name: Bonneville Salt Flats
unique: A 30,000-acre sheet of white salt so flat it looks like water, where land-speed records were set and the horizon bends.
buzz: Go at sunset and walk out until the cars disappear; the salt eats shoes and the glare is brutal. Check conditions after rain.

name: Hell's Revenge 4x4
unique: A slickrock trail over fins and ledges so steep the car seems to fall forward, with a guide who has done it ten thousand times.
buzz: People scream the whole way and book again; driving yourself is allowed but the guided tour is the sane intro. Not for bad backs.

name: Sundance Film Festival
unique: Independent cinema's biggest stage in a ski town, with premieres, Q&As and a Main Street that turns into a deal-making circus in the snow.
buzz: Locals volunteer for free access; tickets are a lottery and the waitlist lines are part of the experience. Book lodging months ahead.

name: Antelope Island Bison
unique: A island in the Great Salt Lake with a free roaming bison herd, bighorn sheep and water so salty you float without trying.
buzz: The bison are everywhere and the lake views are strange and beautiful; bring bug spray in spring. Few crowds.

name: Gilgal Sculpture Garden
unique: A hidden garden of stone carvings by a Mormon bishop, including a sphinx with the face of Joseph Smith, tucked between houses in a residential block.
buzz: It is free, small and genuinely strange; most locals have never been. A five minute detour.
